source.text: אַחֲרֵ֨י הַדְּבָרִ֤ים וְהָאֱמֶת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה בָּ֖א סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיָּבֹ֣א בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וַיִּ֨חַן֙ עַל־הֶעָרִ֣ים הַבְּצֻר֔וֹת וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְבִקְעָ֥ם אֵלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: After the matters and the faithfulness the these came Sennacherib king of Assyria, and he came into Judah and encamped against the cities the fortified, and he said to break them open for himself.

en.L: After these things and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came, and he came into Judah and encamped against the fortified cities, and he thought to break them open for himself.
en.B: After these faithful deeds, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah. He camped against the fortified cities, intending to break into them and take them for himself.
en.R: Hezekiah had done all these things faithfully. After that, King Sennacherib of Assyria came and invaded Judah. He camped outside the walled cities and planned to break through their walls and take them for himself.

es.L: Después de estas cosas y de esta fidelidad, vino Senaquerib rey de Asiria, y entró en Judá y acampó contra las ciudades fortificadas, y pensó abrir brecha en ellas para sí.
es.B: Después de estos hechos de fidelidad, Senaquerib rey de Asiria vino e invadió Judá. Acampó frente a las ciudades fortificadas con la intención de abrir brecha en ellas y tomarlas para sí.
es.R: Ezequías había hecho todas estas cosas con fidelidad. Después de eso, el rey Senaquerib de Asiria vino e invadió Judá. Acampó frente a las ciudades amuralladas y pensaba romper sus murallas y quedarse con ellas.

fr.L: Après ces choses et cette fidélité, Sennachérib, roi d’Assyrie, vint ; et il entra en Juda et campa contre les villes fortifiées, et il pensait les forcer pour lui.
fr.B: Après ces actes de fidélité, Sennachérib, roi d’Assyrie, vint et entra en Juda. Il campa devant les villes fortifiées, avec l’intention d’y pénétrer de force et de les prendre pour lui.
fr.R: Ézéchias avait fait tout cela avec fidélité. Après cela, le roi Sennachérib d’Assyrie est venu envahir Juda. Il a installé son camp devant les villes entourées de murailles, et il voulait percer leurs murailles et les prendre pour lui.

sw.L: Baada ya mambo haya na uaminifu huu, Senakeribu mfalme wa Ashuru akaja, akaingia Yuda, akapiga kambi juu ya miji yenye ngome, akasema [moyoni] kuivunja ili aitwae.
sw.B: Baada ya matendo haya ya uaminifu, Senakeribu mfalme wa Ashuru alikuja akaingia Yuda. Akapiga kambi dhidi ya miji yenye ngome, akikusudia kuivunja na kuiteka iwe yake.
sw.R: Hezekia alikuwa amefanya mambo haya yote kwa uaminifu. Baada ya hayo, mfalme Senakeribu wa Ashuru alikuja akaivamia Yuda. Akapiga kambi nje ya miji yenye kuta, akapanga kuvunja kuta zake na kuiteka iwe yake.

vi.L: Sau những việc ấy và lòng trung tín ấy, San-chê-ríp vua A-si-ri đến, tiến vào Giu-đa và đóng trại đánh các thành kiên cố, và định phá vỡ chúng để chiếm lấy cho mình.
vi.B: Sau những việc làm trung tín ấy, San-chê-ríp vua A-si-ri kéo đến và tiến vào Giu-đa. Vua đóng trại vây các thành kiên cố, định phá vỡ để chiếm lấy cho mình.
vi.R: Ê-xê-chia đã trung tín làm mọi việc ấy. Sau đó, vua San-chê-ríp của A-si-ri kéo đến xâm chiếm Giu-đa. Vua đóng trại bên ngoài các thành có tường bao quanh và tính phá vỡ tường thành để chiếm lấy cho mình.

ko.L: 이런 일들과 이런 신실함이 있은 뒤에, 앗시리아 왕 산헤립이 왔다. 그리고 그가 유다에 들어와 요새 성읍들을 치려고 진을 치고, 그것들을 깨뜨려 자기 것으로 삼으려고 했다.
ko.B: 히스기야가 이렇게 신실하게 일한 뒤에, 앗시리아 왕 산헤립이 유다로 쳐들어왔다. 그는 요새 성읍들을 치려고 진을 치고, 그 성읍들을 깨뜨려 차지하려고 했다.
ko.R: 히스기야는 이 모든 일을 신실하게 했다. 그 뒤에 앗시리아 왕 산헤립이 유다로 쳐들어왔다. 그는 성벽으로 둘러싸인 성읍들 바깥에 진을 쳤다. 그리고 성벽을 뚫고 들어가 그 성읍들을 차지하려고 했다.

pt.L: Depois destas coisas e desta fidelidade, veio Senaqueribe, rei da Assíria, e entrou em Judá, e acampou contra as cidades fortificadas, e pensou em rompê-las para si.
pt.B: Depois desses atos de fidelidade, Senaqueribe, rei da Assíria, veio e entrou em Judá. Acampou contra as cidades fortificadas, com a intenção de rompê-las e tomá-las para si.
pt.R: Ezequias tinha feito tudo isso com fidelidade. Depois disso, Senaqueribe, o rei da Assíria, veio e invadiu Judá. Ele acampou do lado de fora das cidades que tinham muralhas e planejou romper as muralhas e tomá-las para si.

decisions.choice: these things and this faithfulness: these faithful deeds of Hezekiah
decisions.reason: The two nouns are joined and share one "these", so they describe one thing: the acts just told in chapters 29-31, which 31:20-21 sums up as what was good, right and faithful before Yahweh. The writer sets the invasion after Hezekiah's faithfulness, not as a punishment for unfaithfulness.

decisions.choice: Sennacherib's invasion, told more briefly than in 2 Kings 18:13
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 18:13 (and Isaiah 36:1) dates the attack to Hezekiah's fourteenth year and says Sennacherib took all the fortified cities. Chronicles gives no date and says only that he camped against them and meant to break into them; it leaves out Hezekiah's surrender and tribute (2 Kings 18:14-16).

decisions.choice: he said to break them open for himself: he intended to break into them and take them
decisions.reason: "Said" here means said to himself, that is, intended or thought. "Break open" is used of breaching a city wall.

decisions.choice: these faithful deeds
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the two joined nouns as one phrase. Readable says in a clause who was faithful.

decisions.choice: "Senaquerib rey de Asiria"
decisions.reason: The name as the terms note and Spanish 2 Kings 18:13 give it; the account of verses 1-23 reuses the Spanish of 2 Kings 18-19 where the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.choice: "Sennachérib, roi d'Assyrie"
decisions.reason: The name and title as in French 2 Kings 18:13, which this chapter retells in short.

decisions.choice: "San-chê-ríp vua A-si-ri"
decisions.reason: The terms note's form, as the 2 Kings drafts.

decisions.choice: Senaqueribe, rei da Assíria; as cidades fortificadas (L, B), as cidades que tinham muralhas (R)
decisions.reason: Verses 1-24 and 30-33 retell 2 Kings 18-20 more briefly (m2), so the Portuguese takes the words of 2 Kings 18:13 where the Hebrew is the same, "Senaqueribe, rei da Assíria" and "as cidades fortificadas" (Readable "as cidades ... que tinham muralhas"), and drafts the rest from Chronicles' Hebrew; each parallel is named in its verse.

source.text: וַיַּרְא֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּי־בָ֖א סַנְחֵרִ֑יב וּפָנָ֕יו לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Hezekiah that had come Sennacherib, and his face [was] for war against Jerusalem,

en.L: And Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and his face [was set] for war against Jerusalem,
en.B: When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and was set on making war against Jerusalem,
en.R: Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and meant to attack Jerusalem.

es.L: Y Ezequías vio que Senaquerib había venido, y que su rostro [estaba vuelto] a la guerra contra Jerusalén,
es.B: Cuando Ezequías vio que Senaquerib había venido y que estaba decidido a hacer la guerra contra Jerusalén,
es.R: Ezequías vio que Senaquerib había venido y que pensaba atacar Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et Ézéchias vit que Sennachérib était venu et que sa face [était tournée] vers la guerre contre Jérusalem,
fr.B: Quand Ézéchias vit que Sennachérib était venu et qu’il était résolu à faire la guerre à Jérusalem,
fr.R: Ézéchias a vu que Sennachérib était venu et qu’il voulait attaquer Jérusalem.

sw.L: Naye Hezekia alipoona kwamba Senakeribu amekuja, na uso wake [umeelekea] vita juu ya Yerusalemu,
sw.B: Hezekia alipoona kwamba Senakeribu amekuja, naye ameazimu kupigana vita dhidi ya Yerusalemu,
sw.R: Hezekia aliona kwamba Senakeribu amekuja na kwamba alikusudia kuishambulia Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Ê-xê-chia thấy rằng San-chê-ríp đã đến và mặt hắn [hướng] về cuộc chiến chống Giê-ru-sa-lem,
vi.B: Khi Ê-xê-chia thấy San-chê-ríp đã đến và quyết tâm tấn công Giê-ru-sa-lem,
vi.R: Ê-xê-chia thấy San-chê-ríp đã đến và định tấn công Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그리고 히스기야가 산헤립이 왔고 그의 얼굴이 예루살렘을 치려는 전쟁을 [향하고] 있음을 보고,
ko.B: 히스기야는 산헤립이 쳐들어와서 예루살렘을 치려고 마음먹은 것을 보고,
ko.R: 히스기야는 산헤립이 쳐들어와서 예루살렘을 공격하려 한다는 것을 알았다.

pt.L: E Ezequias viu que Senaqueribe tinha vindo e que o seu rosto [estava voltado] para a guerra contra Jerusalém,
pt.B: Quando Ezequias viu que Senaqueribe tinha vindo e estava decidido a guerrear contra Jerusalém,
pt.R: Ezequias viu que Senaqueribe tinha vindo e pretendia atacar Jerusalém.

decisions.choice: his face was for war: he was determined to attack
decisions.reason: To set the face toward something is to turn one's purpose to it. Sennacherib's aim was Jerusalem itself, not only the outlying towns.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 3
decisions.reason: Verse 2 gives the occasion; verse 3 tells what Hezekiah did about it.

decisions.choice: Literal and Balanced end with a comma, so the sentence runs on into verse 3
decisions.reason: As in the English, verse 2 gives the occasion and verse 3 what Hezekiah did (m2); Korean can leave a clause open with "-고," at a verse boundary. Readable closes each verse.

source.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ עִם־שָׂרָיו֙ וְגִבֹּרָ֔יו לִסְתּוֹם֙ אֶת־מֵימֵ֣י הָעֲיָנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִח֣וּץ לָעִ֑יר וַֽיַּעְזְרֽוּהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: and he took counsel with his princes and his mighty [men] to stop up the waters of the springs which [were] from outside to the city, and they helped him.

en.L: and he took counsel with his princes and his mighty men to stop up the waters of the springs that [were] outside the city; and they helped him.
en.B: he consulted with his officials and his warriors about stopping the water of the springs outside the city, and they supported him.
en.R: So he talked with his leaders and his best soldiers. They agreed to block off the springs outside the city, and they helped him do it.

es.L: tomó consejo con sus príncipes y sus valientes para cegar las aguas de las fuentes que [estaban] fuera de la ciudad; y ellos lo ayudaron.
es.B: consultó con sus jefes y sus guerreros sobre cegar las aguas de los manantiales que había fuera de la ciudad, y ellos lo apoyaron.
es.R: Así que habló con sus dirigentes y con sus mejores soldados. Ellos estuvieron de acuerdo en tapar los manantiales que había fuera de la ciudad, y lo ayudaron a hacerlo.

fr.L: et il tint conseil avec ses princes et ses guerriers pour boucher les eaux des sources qui [étaient] en dehors de la ville ; et ils l’aidèrent.
fr.B: il se concerta avec ses chefs et ses guerriers pour boucher les sources qui étaient en dehors de la ville, et ils le soutinrent.
fr.R: Alors il a discuté avec ses chefs et ses meilleurs soldats. Ils ont été d’accord pour boucher les sources qui se trouvaient en dehors de la ville, et ils l’ont aidé à le faire.

sw.L: akafanya shauri pamoja na wakuu wake na mashujaa wake kuyaziba maji ya chemchemi zilizokuwa nje ya mji; nao wakamsaidia.
sw.B: alishauriana na maafisa wake na wapiganaji wake juu ya kuyaziba maji ya chemchemi zilizokuwa nje ya mji, nao wakamuunga mkono.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo alizungumza na viongozi wake na askari wake hodari. Wakakubaliana kuziba chemchemi zilizokuwa nje ya mji, nao wakamsaidia kufanya hivyo.

vi.L: thì vua bàn bạc với các thủ lĩnh và các dũng sĩ của mình để lấp các nguồn nước của các suối ở bên ngoài thành; và họ giúp vua.
vi.B: vua bàn với các quan chức và các chiến binh của mình về việc chặn nước các suối bên ngoài thành, và họ ủng hộ vua.
vi.R: Vì vậy vua bàn với các người lãnh đạo và những binh sĩ giỏi nhất của mình. Họ đồng ý chặn các suối nước bên ngoài thành, và họ giúp vua làm việc đó.

ko.L: 그의 지도자들과 그의 용사들과 의논하여 성 밖에 있는 샘들의 물을 막기로 했다. 그리고 그들이 그를 도왔다.
ko.B: 관리들과 용사들과 의논하여 성 밖에 있는 샘들의 물을 막기로 했다. 그러자 그들이 그를 지지했다.
ko.R: 그래서 그는 지도자들과 가장 뛰어난 군인들과 의논했다. 그들은 성 밖에 있는 샘들을 막기로 뜻을 모으고, 그 일을 도왔다.

pt.L: e tomou conselho com os seus príncipes e os seus valentes para tapar as águas das fontes que [estavam] fora da cidade; e eles o ajudaram.
pt.B: consultou os seus oficiais e os seus guerreiros sobre tapar as fontes de água que ficavam fora da cidade, e eles o apoiaram.
pt.R: Então ele conversou com os seus líderes e os seus melhores soldados. Eles concordaram em fechar as fontes que ficavam fora da cidade e o ajudaram a fazer isso.

decisions.choice: his princes and his mighty men: his court officials and his leading warriors
decisions.reason: *Sarim* are the king's high officials; *gibborim* are proven fighting men. Hezekiah takes advice from both the court and the army.

decisions.choice: stopping the springs outside the city: denying water to a besieging army
decisions.reason: An army camped around a city needed water. By blocking or hiding the springs outside the walls, Hezekiah meant to leave the Assyrians without it (verse 4), while the city kept its own supply (verse 30).

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders; mighty men / warriors / best soldiers
decisions.reason: *Sar* follows the usual table for a king's officials. *Gibborim* is "mighty men" at Literal and is named by what they were at the other levels.

decisions.choice: "príncipes" / "jefes" / "dirigentes"; "valientes" (L); "guerreros" (B); "mejores soldados" (R)
decisions.reason: The officials keep one word per level through the block; the mighty men are named by what they were at Balanced and Readable, as the English does.

decisions.choice: príncipes (L), oficiais (B), líderes (R); valentes (L), guerreiros (B), melhores soldados (R)
decisions.reason: The king's officials take the three words used through the book (30:2); the proven fighting men (m1) are "valentes" at Literal, the old word for mighty men, and are named by what they were at Balanced and Readable, as the English.

source.text: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ עַם־רָ֔ב וַֽיִּסְתְּמוּ֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַמַּעְיָנ֔וֹת וְאֶת־הַנַּ֛חַל הַשּׁוֹטֵ֥ף בְּתוֹךְ־הָאָ֖רֶץ לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֤מָּה יָב֨וֹאוּ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י אַשּׁ֔וּר וּמָצְא֖וּ מַ֥יִם רַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And were gathered people many, and they stopped up all the springs and the wadi the flowing in [the] midst of the land, saying, why should come [the] kings of Assyria and find waters many?

en.L: And many people were gathered, and they stopped up all the springs and the brook that flowed through the midst of the land, saying, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find much water?"
en.B: A great many people gathered and blocked all the springs and the stream running across the land. "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find water in plenty?" they said.
en.R: Many people came together and blocked all the springs and the stream that ran through the land. They said, "Why should the kings of Assyria come here and find plenty of water?"

es.L: Y se reunió mucha gente, y cegaron todas las fuentes y el arroyo que corría por en medio de la tierra, diciendo: «¿Por qué han de venir los reyes de Asiria y hallar muchas aguas?».
es.B: Se reunió muchísima gente, y taparon todos los manantiales y el arroyo que atravesaba la región. «¿Por qué han de venir los reyes de Asiria y encontrar agua en abundancia?», decían.
es.R: Mucha gente se juntó y tapó todos los manantiales y el arroyo que pasaba por la región. Decían: «¿Por qué tienen que venir los reyes de Asiria y encontrar agua en abundancia?».

fr.L: Et beaucoup de gens se rassemblèrent, et ils bouchèrent toutes les sources et le torrent qui coulait au milieu du pays, en disant : « Pourquoi les rois d’Assyrie viendraient-ils et trouveraient-ils beaucoup d’eau ? »
fr.B: Une foule nombreuse se rassembla et boucha toutes les sources et le cours d’eau qui traversait le pays. « Pourquoi les rois d’Assyrie trouveraient-ils de l’eau en abondance en arrivant ? » disaient-ils.
fr.R: Beaucoup de gens se sont réunis et ils ont bouché toutes les sources et le ruisseau qui traversait le pays. Ils disaient : « Pourquoi les rois d’Assyrie trouveraient-ils beaucoup d’eau en venant ici ? »

sw.L: Watu wengi wakakusanyika, wakaziba chemchemi zote na kijito kilichotiririka katikati ya nchi, wakisema, "Kwa nini wafalme wa Ashuru waje na kukuta maji mengi?"
sw.B: Watu wengi sana walikusanyika wakaziba chemchemi zote na kijito kilichopita katikati ya nchi. Wakasema, "Kwa nini wafalme wa Ashuru waje na kukuta maji mengi?"
sw.R: Watu wengi walikusanyika, wakaziba chemchemi zote na kijito kilichopita katika nchi. Wakasema, "Kwa nini wafalme wa Ashuru waje hapa na kukuta maji mengi?"

vi.L: Rất đông người nhóm lại, lấp hết các suối và dòng suối chảy qua giữa xứ, mà nói: "Sao để các vua A-si-ri đến và tìm được nhiều nước?"
vi.B: Rất đông người tụ họp lại và chặn hết các suối cùng dòng suối chảy ngang qua xứ. Họ nói: "Sao lại để các vua A-si-ri đến mà có nước dồi dào?"
vi.R: Nhiều người tụ họp lại và chặn hết các suối và dòng suối chảy qua xứ. Họ nói: "Sao lại để các vua A-si-ri đến đây mà có nhiều nước?"

ko.L: 그리고 많은 백성이 모여서 모든 샘과 그 땅 가운데로 흐르는 시내를 막으며 말했다. "어찌하여 앗시리아 왕들이 와서 많은 물을 얻게 하겠느냐?"
ko.B: 많은 백성이 모여서 모든 샘과 그 땅을 가로질러 흐르는 시내를 막았다. 그들이 말했다. "어찌 앗시리아 왕들이 와서 물을 넉넉히 얻게 하겠느냐?"
ko.R: 많은 사람이 모여서 모든 샘과 그 땅을 흐르는 시냇물을 막았다. 그들이 말했다. "앗시리아 왕들이 여기에 와서 물을 실컷 얻게 할 까닭이 어디 있겠느냐?"

pt.L: E muito povo se reuniu, e taparam todas as fontes e o ribeiro que corria pelo meio da terra, dizendo: "Por que viriam os reis da Assíria e achariam muitas águas?"
pt.B: Muita gente se reuniu e tapou todas as fontes e o riacho que corria pela região. "Por que os reis da Assíria haveriam de vir e encontrar água em abundância?", diziam.
pt.R: Muita gente se reuniu e fechou todas as fontes e o riacho que corria pela região. Eles disseram: "Por que os reis da Assíria haveriam de vir aqui e encontrar água à vontade?"

decisions.choice: the brook that flowed through the land: probably the stream fed by the Gihon spring in the Kidron Valley
decisions.reason: The text does not name it. The only large spring at Jerusalem was the Gihon, in the valley east of the City of David, and verse 30 tells how Hezekiah stopped its upper outlet. The stream is most likely the overflow from that spring running down the valley.

decisions.choice: the kings of Assyria: the Assyrian king and his forces, or Assyrian kings in general
decisions.reason: The plural may speak of Assyria's kings as a type, since they had come before (28:16, 20), or include the vassal kings who marched with Sennacherib. Either way the danger meant is the present invasion.

records.literal_gloss: And he strengthened himself and built all the wall the broken down, and raised [it] on the towers, and outside [it] the wall another, and he strengthened the Millo [of the] city of David, and made weapon[s] in abundance and shields.

en.L: And he strengthened himself and built all the wall that was broken down, and raised [it] up on the towers, and outside [it] another wall; and he strengthened the Millo [in] the City of David, and made weapons in abundance, and shields.
en.B: Hezekiah took courage. He rebuilt all the wall where it was broken down and raised it up to the towers, and he built another wall outside it. He strengthened the Millo in the City of David and made large numbers of weapons and shields.
en.R: Hezekiah went to work with courage. He repaired every broken part of the city wall and built it up as high as the towers. He built a second wall outside the first one. He made the Millo (a supporting terrace) in the City of David stronger. He also made many weapons and shields.

es.L: Y se esforzó, y reedificó todo el muro que estaba derribado, y [lo] alzó hasta las torres, y otro muro por fuera; y fortificó el Milo [de] la ciudad de David, e hizo armas en abundancia y escudos.
es.B: Ezequías cobró ánimo. Reconstruyó todo el muro donde estaba derribado y lo levantó hasta las torres, y construyó otro muro por fuera. Fortificó el Milo en la ciudad de David e hizo gran cantidad de armas y escudos.
es.R: Ezequías se puso a trabajar con valor. Reparó todas las partes rotas de la muralla de la ciudad y la levantó hasta la altura de las torres. Construyó una segunda muralla por fuera de la primera. Hizo más fuerte el Milo (una terraza de apoyo) en la ciudad de David. También hizo muchas armas y escudos.

fr.L: Et il s’affermit, et il rebâtit toute la muraille qui était en brèche, et l’éleva jusqu’aux tours, et au-dehors une autre muraille ; et il fortifia le Millo de la cité de David, et il fit des armes en abondance, et des boucliers.
fr.B: Ézéchias prit courage. Il rebâtit toute la muraille là où elle était en brèche et l’éleva jusqu’aux tours, puis il construisit une autre muraille à l’extérieur. Il fortifia le Millo dans la cité de David et fit fabriquer une grande quantité d’armes et de boucliers.
fr.R: Ézéchias s’est mis au travail avec courage. Il a réparé toutes les parties de la muraille de la ville qui étaient abîmées, et il l’a élevée jusqu’à la hauteur des tours. Il a construit une deuxième muraille à l’extérieur de la première. Il a renforcé le Millo (une terrasse de soutien) dans la cité de David. Il a aussi fait fabriquer beaucoup d’armes et de boucliers.

sw.L: Akajitia nguvu, akaujenga ukuta wote uliobomoka, akaupandisha juu ya minara, na nje [yake] ukuta mwingine; akaiimarisha Milo [katika] mji wa Daudi, akatengeneza silaha kwa wingi, na ngao.
sw.B: Hezekia alipiga moyo konde. Aliujenga upya ukuta wote mahali ulipobomoka, akaupandisha mpaka kufikia minara, akajenga ukuta mwingine nje yake. Akaiimarisha Milo katika mji wa Daudi, akatengeneza silaha nyingi na ngao.
sw.R: Hezekia alianza kazi kwa ujasiri. Alitengeneza kila sehemu iliyobomoka ya ukuta wa mji, akaujenga juu mpaka kufikia urefu wa minara. Akajenga ukuta wa pili nje ya ule wa kwanza. Akaifanya Milo (jukwaa la kutegemeza majengo) katika mji wa Daudi kuwa imara zaidi. Pia akatengeneza silaha nyingi na ngao.

vi.L: Vua làm cho mình vững mạnh, xây lại tất cả đoạn tường thành đã đổ, nâng [nó] lên đến các tháp, và xây một bức tường khác bên ngoài; vua củng cố Mi-lô [trong] thành Đa-vít, và làm rất nhiều vũ khí và khiên.
vi.B: Ê-xê-chia lấy can đảm. Vua xây lại tất cả những chỗ tường thành bị đổ và nâng tường lên cao đến các tháp, rồi xây thêm một bức tường khác bên ngoài. Vua củng cố Mi-lô trong thành Đa-vít và làm rất nhiều vũ khí và khiên.
vi.R: Ê-xê-chia can đảm bắt tay vào việc. Vua sửa lại mọi chỗ tường thành bị đổ và xây cao lên ngang các tháp. Vua xây thêm bức tường thứ hai bên ngoài bức tường thứ nhất. Vua làm cho Mi-lô (một nền đất đắp cao để đỡ các công trình) trong thành Đa-vít vững chắc hơn. Vua cũng làm nhiều vũ khí và khiên.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 힘을 내어, 무너진 성벽을 모두 쌓고, 망대들 위까지 높이 올리고, 그 바깥에 다른 성벽을 [쌓았다]. 그리고 그가 다윗 성의 밀로를 견고하게 하고, 무기와 방패를 많이 만들었다.
ko.B: 히스기야는 용기를 내어 무너진 성벽을 모두 다시 쌓고, 망대 높이까지 쌓아 올렸다. 그리고 그 바깥에 성벽을 하나 더 쌓았다. 그는 다윗 성의 밀로를 견고하게 하고, 무기와 방패를 많이 만들었다.
ko.R: 히스기야는 용기를 내어 일했다. 그는 성벽에서 무너진 곳을 모두 고치고, 망대 높이만큼 쌓아 올렸다. 그리고 바깥에 성벽을 하나 더 쌓았다. 그는 다윗 성에 있는 밀로(건물들을 받치는 축대)를 더 튼튼하게 했다. 또 무기와 방패도 많이 만들었다.

pt.L: E ele se fortaleceu, e reconstruiu todo o muro que estava derrubado, e [o] ergueu até as torres, e fora [dele] outro muro; e fortaleceu o Milo [na] Cidade de Davi, e fez armas em abundância e escudos.
pt.B: Ezequias criou coragem. Reconstruiu todo o muro onde estava derrubado e o ergueu até a altura das torres, e construiu outro muro do lado de fora. Reforçou o Milo na Cidade de Davi e fez grande quantidade de armas e escudos.
pt.R: Ezequias começou o trabalho com coragem. Consertou todas as partes quebradas do muro da cidade e o levantou até a altura das torres. Construiu um segundo muro do lado de fora do primeiro. Reforçou o Milo (um grande aterro de sustentação) na Cidade de Davi. Também fez muitas armas e escudos.

decisions.choice: he strengthened himself: he took courage and acted with resolve
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of a king who sets himself firmly to a task (1:1; 15:8). It describes his resolve, which shows in the work that follows.

decisions.choice: raised [it] up on the towers: built the wall up to the height of its towers
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "he raised on the towers", with no object. Read as it stands, the wall itself is raised to the towers. A small change to the text gives "he raised towers on it", which some early translations seem to reflect. Either way the walls were made higher and stronger.

decisions.choice: the Millo: a terrace or filled-in structure supporting buildings in the City of David
decisions.reason: The name comes from a word for filling. David and Solomon built it (1 Chronicles 11:8; 1 Kings 9:15); it was part of the defenses of the old city on the eastern hill.

decisions.choice: weapons: arms for throwing or thrusting, such as spears and javelins
decisions.reason: The word is used of weapons in general and of missiles. Together with shields it means Hezekiah equipped the defenders.

decisions.choice: the Millo (a supporting terrace)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name, as 1 Kings 9:15 does.

decisions.choice: "el Milo (una terraza de apoyo)"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name, as the English does; "Milo" as Spanish 1 Kings 9:15.

decisions.choice: o Milo; o Milo (um grande aterro de sustentação) (R)
decisions.reason: The name (m3) and Readable's explanation keep the words 1 Kings 9:15 has in Portuguese. "Se fortaleceu" (L) keeps the verb of 1:1 (m1); Balanced and Readable say "criou coragem" and "com coragem", as the English.

decisions.choice: commanders of war over the people: officers set over the men of the city as fighters
decisions.reason: *'Am* here is the population of Jerusalem organized for its defense. *Sarim* in this military setting are commanders.

decisions.choice: the square of the city gate: the open space inside a gate, used for gatherings
decisions.reason: City gates had open areas where people met, trade was done and announcements made (Nehemiah 8:1).

decisions.choice: he spoke to their heart: he encouraged them
decisions.reason: To speak to someone's heart is to speak kindly so as to reassure or encourage (Genesis 50:21; Isaiah 40:2). Here it means strengthening their courage, as 30:22 uses it for words of encouragement.

decisions.choice: falou ao coração deles (L); lhes falou com palavras de ânimo (B); o encorajou (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom (m3) takes the words 30:22 uses for it in Portuguese at each level.

records.literal_gloss: Be strong and be bold; do not fear and do not be dismayed because of [the] king of Assyria and because of all the multitude which [is] with him, for with us [is] more than with him.

en.L: "Be strong and bold. Do not fear, and do not be dismayed because of the king of Assyria and because of all the multitude that [is] with him, for with us [is] more than with him.
en.B: "Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged because of the king of Assyria and all the horde that is with him, for there is more on our side than on his.
en.R: "Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid. Do not lose heart because of the king of Assyria and the huge army with him. We have more on our side than he has.

es.L: «{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fuertes y valerosos; no {{plural_you:teman|temáis}} ni se {{plural_you:acobarden|acobardéis}} a causa del rey de Asiria ni a causa de toda la multitud que [está] con él, porque con nosotros [hay] más que con él.
es.B: «{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fuertes y valientes. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo ni se {{plural_you:desanimen|desaniméis}} a causa del rey de Asiria ni de toda la multitud que lo acompaña, porque de nuestro lado hay más que del suyo.
es.R: «{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fuertes y valientes. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. No {{plural_you:pierdan|perdáis}} el ánimo por causa del rey de Asiria y del enorme ejército que lo acompaña. De nuestro lado hay más que del suyo.

fr.L: « Soyez forts et courageux ! Ne craignez pas et ne soyez pas effrayés à cause du roi d’Assyrie et à cause de toute la multitude qui [est] avec lui, car avec nous [il y a] plus qu’avec lui.
fr.B: « Soyez forts et courageux ! N’ayez pas peur et ne vous laissez pas abattre à cause du roi d’Assyrie et de toute la foule qui l’accompagne, car il y a plus de notre côté que du sien.
fr.R: « Soyez forts et courageux ! N’ayez pas peur. Ne perdez pas courage à cause du roi d’Assyrie et de l’énorme armée qui est avec lui. Il y a plus de notre côté que du sien.

sw.L: "Iweni hodari na moyo mkuu; msiogope wala msifadhaike kwa sababu ya mfalme wa Ashuru na kwa sababu ya umati wote ulio pamoja naye, kwa maana walio pamoja nasi [ni] wengi kuliko walio pamoja naye.
sw.B: "Iweni hodari na jasiri. Msiogope wala msikate tamaa kwa sababu ya mfalme wa Ashuru na kundi lote kubwa lililo pamoja naye, kwa maana aliye upande wetu ni mkuu kuliko walio upande wake.
sw.R: "Iweni hodari na mashujaa. Msiogope. Msife moyo kwa sababu ya mfalme wa Ashuru na jeshi kubwa lililo pamoja naye. Aliye upande wetu ni mkuu kuliko walio upande wake.

vi.L: "Hãy mạnh mẽ và can đảm! Đừng sợ và đừng kinh hãi trước vua A-si-ri và trước cả đoàn quân đông đảo đi với hắn, vì có [Đấng] ở với chúng ta lớn hơn kẻ ở với hắn.
vi.B: "Hãy mạnh mẽ và can đảm! Đừng sợ hãi hay nản lòng trước vua A-si-ri và cả đám quân đông đảo đi với hắn, vì bên chúng ta có Đấng lớn hơn bên hắn.
vi.R: "Hãy mạnh mẽ và dũng cảm. Đừng sợ. Đừng nản lòng trước vua A-si-ri và đạo quân đông đảo đi với hắn. Bên chúng ta có Đấng mạnh hơn bên hắn.

ko.L: "강하고 담대하여라. 앗시리아 왕과 그와 함께 있는 모든 무리 때문에 두려워하지 말고 낙심하지 마라. 우리와 함께하는 이가 그와 함께하는 자보다 더 크기 때문이다.
ko.B: "강하고 담대하여라. 앗시리아 왕과 그와 함께 있는 저 큰 무리 때문에 두려워하지도 말고 낙심하지도 마라. 우리 편에 계신 분이 그의 편에 있는 자들보다 더 크시다.
ko.R: "강하고 용감하여라. 앗시리아 왕과 그와 함께 온 엄청난 군대 때문에 두려워하지 마라. 용기를 잃지 마라. 우리 편이 그의 편보다 더 크다.

pt.L: "Sejam fortes e corajosos; não temam e não se apavorem por causa do rei da Assíria e por causa de toda a multidão que [está] com ele, porque conosco [há] mais do que com ele.
pt.B: "Sejam fortes e corajosos. Não tenham medo nem percam o ânimo por causa do rei da Assíria e de toda a multidão que está com ele, porque há mais do nosso lado do que do lado dele.
pt.R: "Sejam fortes e corajosos. Não tenham medo. Não percam o ânimo por causa do rei da Assíria e do enorme exército que está com ele. Há mais do nosso lado do que do lado dele.

decisions.choice: be strong and bold, do not fear or be dismayed: the words spoken to Joshua and to Israel before battle
decisions.reason: Hezekiah uses the charge Moses gave Israel and Joshua (Deuteronomy 31:6-8), which Yahweh repeated to Joshua (Joshua 1:9) and Joshua gave the army (Joshua 10:25). David used it for Solomon (1 Chronicles 22:13; 28:20). The king calls on the promise behind it, that Yahweh goes with his people.

decisions.choice: with us is more than with him: one greater, as verse 8 explains
alternatives: there are more with us than with him
decisions.reason: The word for "more" is singular and can mean "one greater". Verse 8 makes clear what Hezekiah means: Assyria has only human strength, while Judah has Yahweh. The saying recalls Elisha's words at Dothan (2 Kings 6:16).

decisions.choice: the multitude: a great, noisy crowd, here the Assyrian army
decisions.reason: The word suggests both size and noise, as the great army that came against Jehoshaphat (20:2, 12, 15).

decisions.choice: be strong and bold / be strong and courageous / be strong and brave
decisions.reason: The same wording as in Joshua at each level, so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: more on our side
decisions.reason: "Side" is supplied to make the comparison clear; "more" keeps the Hebrew's openness about whether it means numbers or power.

decisions.choice: "Sean fuertes y valerosos" (L); "Sean fuertes y valientes" (B, R); plural_you
decisions.reason: The words spoken to Joshua (m1) keep the wording of the published Spanish Joshua 1:6-9, "Sé fuerte y valeroso" (L) and "Sé fuerte y valiente" (B, R), so the echo is heard; Hezekiah speaks to all the people, so every "you" is plural.

decisions.choice: "Soyez forts et courageux" at every level
decisions.reason: One wording at every level so the echo of Joshua 1 is heard (m1); the "do not fear ... be dismayed" pair as in 20:15.

decisions.choice: Iweni hodari na moyo mkuu / hodari na jasiri / hodari na mashujaa
decisions.reason: The charge echoes Moses' words to Joshua (m1); each level keeps one wording for the pair, so the echo can be heard.

decisions.choice: "[Đấng] ở với chúng ta" (L); "Đấng lớn hơn" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "more is with us"; verse 8 shows that the one with them is God (m2), so Vietnamese supplies "Đấng", the word for a divine person.

decisions.choice: "강하고 담대하여라 ... 두려워하지 말고 낙심하지 마라"
decisions.reason: The charge to Joshua (m1) is worded as Jahaziel's message at 20:15 and 17, so the echo is heard within this block; the king speaks to his people in 해라체.

decisions.choice: Sejam fortes e corajosos; não temam e não se apavorem (L), Não tenham medo nem percam o ânimo (B, R)
decisions.reason: Hezekiah uses the charge given to Joshua and the army (m1), so each level takes the Portuguese of Joshua 10:25, the same charge in the plural, as the English keeps its Joshua wording. "Mais" keeps the Hebrew's openness (m2), as 2 Kings 6:16 does in Portuguese.

en.L: With him [is] an arm of flesh, but with us [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, to help us and to fight our battles." And the people leaned on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

decisions.choice: an arm of flesh: mere human strength
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength and "flesh" for what is human and weak, set against God. Jeremiah 17:5 uses the same picture of trusting in human power instead of Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Yahweh our God, to help us and to fight our battles
decisions.reason: Hezekiah's confidence rests on Yahweh as the one who fights for his people, as at the Red Sea (Exodus 14:14) and in Jehoshaphat's day (20:15, 17).

decisions.choice: leaned on: relied on, took support from
decisions.reason: The verb means to lean or rest one's weight on something. The people's courage rested on what the king had told them.

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: "Only" brings out the contrast the Hebrew makes by setting the two clauses side by side; Balanced and Readable also add "for us" to the battles.

decisions.choice: human strength
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the arm of flesh.

decisions.choice: "fuerza humana"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the arm of flesh (m1); Literal and Balanced keep it.

decisions.choice: "육신의 팔" at Literal

decisions.choice: um braço de carne (L, B); só a força humana (R); se apoiou (L), ganhou confiança (B), ficou animado (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture (m1), "braço de carne", which Portuguese readers know from the prophets and can follow as human strength set against God; Readable says what it means, as the English. Literal keeps the verb of leaning (m3).

decisions.choice: Sennacherib's envoys from Lachish: 2 Kings 18:17
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 18:17 (and Isaiah 36:2) names three high officers and says they came with a large army and stood by the conduit of the Upper Pool. Chronicles calls them only "his servants" and does not name them or say where they stood.

decisions.choice: he was at Lachish: he was besieging Lachish
decisions.reason: "At" or "against" Lachish means he was laying siege to it. Lachish was the strongest town of Judah after Jerusalem, about thirty miles southwest of it.

decisions.choice: all his dominion: all his royal forces
decisions.reason: The word means rule or dominion; here, as in Jeremiah 34:1, it stands for the forces of his empire with him.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: *'Eved* used of a king's envoys is "servants" at Literal and "officials" at Balanced and Readable, as in 2 Kings 18-19.

decisions.choice: "sus siervos" (L); "sus funcionarios" (B, R)
decisions.reason: A king's envoys are "siervos" at Literal and "funcionarios" at Balanced and Readable, as in Spanish 2 Kings 18:17.

decisions.choice: "serviteurs" (Literal); "officiers" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The king's servants as in French Kings, here Sennacherib's envoys.

decisions.choice: the narrator calls Sennacherib "hắn" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As the 2 Kings drafts do for an enemy king who mocks God; Literal and the first mention keep his title.

decisions.choice: os seus servos (L), os seus oficiais (B, R); Laquis
alternatives: o Tartã, o Rabe-Sáris e o Rabsaqué
decisions.reason: Chronicles does not name the three officers of 2 Kings 18:17 (m1), so the Portuguese does not bring in their titles; the envoys are "servos" at Literal and "oficiais" at Balanced and Readable, as the English, and the town keeps the Portuguese of 2 Kings 18:17, "Laquis". The Assyrian speaks to the people in verses 10-15, so he says "vocês", where 2 Kings 18:19-21 has him speak to Hezekiah with "você".

pt.R: "É isto que o rei Senaqueribe, da Assíria, diz: Por que vocês se sentem tão seguros? O que faz vocês ficarem em Jerusalém enquanto ela está cercada?

decisions.choice: what are you trusting in?: the Rabshakeh's opening question, 2 Kings 18:19-20
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 18:19-20 (Isaiah 36:4-5) the speech opens with "What is this trust that you trust?" and "On whom do you rely?". Chronicles gives a shorter form of the same challenge and adds the siege.

decisions.choice: in siege: shut in under siege
decisions.reason: The word means siege, or a place under siege. The Assyrians present Jerusalem's people as already trapped. 2 Kings does not say Jerusalem was formally besieged, and the word may describe the threat as much as an army already dug in around the walls.

decisions.choice: Thus says / ... says this / This is what ... says
decisions.reason: The messenger formula has the same wording as in 2 Kings 18:19 at each level.

decisions.choice: two questions
decisions.reason: Readable splits the one question into two short ones.

decisions.choice: "Así dice" (L); "dice esto" (B); "Esto es lo que dice" (R); plural_you
decisions.reason: The messenger formula as in Spanish 2 Kings 18:19. The message goes to Hezekiah and all Judah, so every "you" in verses 10-15 is plural.

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle" (Literal); "dit ceci" (Balanced); "Voici ce que dit" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula of the Assyrian king takes the wording of French 2 Kings 18:19; here addressed to the people ("vous").

decisions.choice: Senakeribu ... asema hivi (L); Hivi ndivyo asemavyo Senakeribu (B); Hili ndilo Senakeribu analosema (R)
alternatives: Hivi ndivyo asemavyo mfalme (L, as the 2 Kings 18 draft)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula follows the pattern set for "Thus says the LORD" in this block; the 2 Kings 13-25 drafts word the Rabshakeh's formula in another order, for a reviewer to harmonise.

decisions.choice: "phán thế này" (L); "phán như vầy" (B); "Đây là lời ..." (R) for the Assyrian king
decisions.reason: The 2 Kings drafts give the great king's message with "phán", echoing the prophets' formula as the Hebrew does (uncertain there too); "các ngươi" for the people.

decisions.choice: The Assyrian message in 해라체, with the messenger formula of 2 Kings 18:19 for the Assyrian king ("이와 같이 말한다", "이렇게 말한다", "... 말이다")
decisions.reason: As in the Kings drafts, Sennacherib's envoys speak down to Judah, and in their mouths Yahweh is named without the honorific (verses 11-17).

decisions.choice: Assim diz (L, B), É isto que ... diz (R); confiando (L), se apoiando (B), se sentem tão seguros (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula and the challenge keep the Portuguese of 2 Kings 18:19-20 at each level (m1): "Assim diz" and "É isto que ... diz", "confiar" at Literal, "se apoiar" at Balanced and "se sentir seguro" at Readable.

source.text: הֲלֹ֤א יְחִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ מַסִּ֣ית אֶתְכֶ֔ם לָתֵ֣ת אֶתְכֶ֔ם לָמ֛וּת בְּרָעָ֥ב וּבְצָמָ֖א לֵאמֹ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ יַצִּילֵ֕נוּ מִכַּ֖ף מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] not Hezekiah misleading you to give you to die by hunger and by thirst, saying, Yahweh our God will deliver us from [the] palm of [the] king of Assyria?

en.L: Is not Hezekiah misleading you, to give you over to die by famine and by thirst, saying, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God will deliver us from the palm of the king of Assyria'?
en.B: Is Hezekiah not misleading you, handing you over to die of hunger and thirst, when he says, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God will rescue us from the power of the king of Assyria'?
en.R: Hezekiah is fooling you. He says, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God will save us from the king of Assyria.' But he is leading you to die of hunger and thirst.

es.L: ¿No {{plural_you:los|os}} engaña Ezequías, para entregar{{plural_you:los|os}} a morir de hambre y de sed, diciendo: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios nos librará de la mano del rey de Asiria”?
es.B: ¿No {{plural_you:los|os}} está engañando Ezequías, entregándo{{plural_you:los|os}} a morir de hambre y de sed, cuando dice: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios nos librará del poder del rey de Asiria”?
es.R: Ezequías {{plural_you:los|os}} está engañando. Él dice: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios nos salvará del rey de Asiria”. Pero {{plural_you:los|os}} está llevando a morir de hambre y de sed.

fr.L: Ézéchias ne vous égare-t-il pas, pour vous livrer à la mort par la faim et par la soif, en disant : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu nous délivrera de la main du roi d’Assyrie” ?
fr.B: Ézéchias ne vous égare-t-il pas ? Il vous livre à la mort par la faim et la soif quand il vous dit : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu nous délivrera de la main du roi d’Assyrie.”
fr.R: Ézéchias vous trompe. Il vous dit : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu nous sauvera du roi d’Assyrie.” Mais il vous conduit à mourir de faim et de soif.

sw.L: Je, Hezekia hawapotoshi ninyi, ili awatoe mfe kwa njaa na kwa kiu, akisema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu atatuokoa kutoka kiganjani mwa mfalme wa Ashuru'?
sw.B: Je, Hezekia hawapotoshi, akiwatoa mfe kwa njaa na kiu, anaposema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu atatuokoa kutoka mkononi mwa mfalme wa Ashuru'?
sw.R: Hezekia anawadanganya. Anasema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu atatuokoa kutoka kwa mfalme wa Ashuru.' Lakini anawaongoza mfe kwa njaa na kiu.

vi.L: Chẳng phải Ê-xê-chia đang dụ dỗ các ngươi, để nộp các ngươi cho chết vì đói và khát, khi nói: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta, sẽ giải cứu chúng ta khỏi tay vua A-si-ri' sao?
vi.B: Chẳng phải Ê-xê-chia đang dụ dỗ các ngươi, nộp các ngươi cho chết đói chết khát, khi hắn nói: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta, sẽ giải cứu chúng ta khỏi quyền lực của vua A-si-ri' sao?
vi.R: Ê-xê-chia đang lừa các ngươi. Hắn nói: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta, sẽ cứu chúng ta khỏi vua A-si-ri.' Nhưng hắn đang dẫn các ngươi đến chỗ chết đói chết khát.

ko.L: 히스기야가 '우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 앗시리아 왕의 손바닥에서 우리를 건져 낼 것이다' 하고 말하면서, 너희를 굶주림과 목마름으로 죽게 내주려고 너희를 꾀고 있는 것이 아니냐?
ko.B: 히스기야가 '우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 앗시리아 왕의 손에서 우리를 구해 낼 것이다' 하고 말하지만, 그것은 너희를 꾀어 굶주림과 목마름으로 죽게 하려는 것이 아니냐?
ko.R: 히스기야는 너희를 속이고 있다. 그는 '우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 앗시리아 왕에게서 우리를 구해 낼 것이다' 하고 말한다. 그러나 그는 너희를 굶주림과 목마름으로 죽게 만들고 있다.

pt.L: Não [é] Ezequias [que] os está iludindo, para entregá-los à morte pela fome e pela sede, dizendo: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o nosso Deus, nos livrará da palma do rei da Assíria'?
pt.B: Ezequias não está iludindo vocês, entregando-os à morte de fome e de sede, quando diz: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o nosso Deus, vai nos livrar do poder do rei da Assíria'?
pt.R: Ezequias está enganando vocês. Ele diz: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o nosso Deus, vai nos salvar do rei da Assíria.' Mas ele está levando vocês a morrer de fome e de sede.

decisions.choice: Hezekiah misleads you, saying Yahweh will deliver us: 2 Kings 18:30, 32
decisions.reason: The same charge as in 2 Kings 18:30, 32, with the same verb for "mislead". Chronicles adds that by holding out, the people will die of hunger and thirst, which 2 Kings 18:27 says more coarsely.

decisions.choice: from the palm of: from the power of
decisions.reason: "Palm" or "hand" stands for grip and control.

decisions.choice: is not Hezekiah ...?: a question expecting the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question is an accusation.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: Readable states the accusation outright and puts Hezekiah's words before the result.

decisions.choice: "우리 하나님 주가 ... 건져 낼 것이다", Hezekiah's words quoted by the Assyrian without the honorific
decisions.reason: The words are Hezekiah's, but they are put in the enemy's mouth, and the Kings drafts give Yahweh no honorific when the Assyrians speak (2 Kings 18:35).

decisions.choice: iludir (L, B), enganar (R); livrar (L, B), salvar (R)
decisions.reason: "Livrar" (L, B) and "salvar" (R) are the key verb of 2 Kings 18:29-35 in Portuguese, kept through verses 11-17. 2 Kings 18:29, 32 says "enganar" for both verbs of deceiving; Chronicles sets them side by side in verse 15, so Literal and Balanced keep "enganar" for the verb of 2 Kings 18:29 and say "iludir" for this one (m1), and Readable says "enganar", the plain word.

source.text: הֲלֹא־הוּא֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ הֵסִ֥יר אֶת־בָּמֹתָ֖יו וְאֶת־מִזְבְּחֹתָ֑יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לִֽיהוּדָ֤ה וְלִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לִפְנֵ֨י מִזְבֵּ֧חַ אֶחָ֛ד תִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ וְעָלָ֥יו תַּקְטִֽירוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] not he, Hezekiah, [who] removed his high places and his altars, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, saying, before altar one you will bow down and on it you will make smoke?

en.L: Did not this Hezekiah remove {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} high places and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} altars, and say to Judah and to Jerusalem, 'Before one altar you shall bow down, and on it you shall make [offerings] smoke'?
en.B: Did this same Hezekiah not get rid of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} high places and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} altars and tell Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must bow down before one altar and burn your offerings on it'?
en.R: Hezekiah himself tore down {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s hilltop shrines and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} altars. He told the people of Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship at only one altar and burn your offerings only on it.'

es.L: ¿No es este Ezequías el que quitó {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} lugares altos y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} altares, y dijo a Judá y a Jerusalén: “Delante de un solo altar {{plural_you:se postrarán|os postraréis}}, y sobre él {{plural_you:quemarán|quemaréis}} [las ofrendas]”?
es.B: ¿No fue este mismo Ezequías el que quitó {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} lugares altos y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} altares, y les dijo a Judá y a Jerusalén: “{{plural_you:Deben postrarse|Debéis postraros}} delante de un solo altar y quemar sobre él {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} ofrendas”?
es.R: Ezequías mismo derribó los santuarios {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} sobre las colinas y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} altares. Les dijo a la gente de Judá y de Jerusalén: “{{plural_you:Deben|Debéis}} adorar ante un solo altar y quemar {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} ofrendas solo sobre él”.

fr.L: N’est-ce pas lui, Ézéchias, qui a ôté {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} hauts lieux et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} autels, et qui a dit à Juda et à Jérusalem : “Devant un seul autel vous vous prosternerez, et sur lui vous ferez fumer [les offrandes]” ?
fr.B: N’est-ce pas ce même Ézéchias qui a fait disparaître {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} hauts lieux et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} autels, et qui a dit à Juda et à Jérusalem : “Vous vous prosternerez devant un seul autel et c’est sur lui que vous brûlerez vos offrandes” ?
fr.R: Ézéchias lui-même a démoli les sanctuaires {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sur les collines et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} autels. Il a dit aux gens de Juda et de Jérusalem : “Vous devez adorer devant un seul autel et brûler vos offrandes seulement sur lui.”

sw.L: Je, si yeye Hezekia aliyeondoa mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} pa juu na madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, akawaambia Yuda na Yerusalemu, akisema, 'Mbele ya madhabahu moja mtasujudu, na juu yake mtafukiza [sadaka]'?
sw.B: Je, si Hezekia huyo huyo aliyeondoa mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} pa juu na madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, akawaambia Yuda na Yerusalemu, 'Ni lazima msujudu mbele ya madhabahu moja na kuteketeza sadaka zenu juu yake'?
sw.R: Hezekia mwenyewe alibomoa patakatifu pa kilimani pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Aliwaambia watu wa Yuda na Yerusalemu, 'Ni lazima mwabudu kwenye madhabahu moja tu na kuteketeza sadaka zenu juu yake tu.'

vi.L: Chẳng phải chính Ê-xê-chia này đã dẹp bỏ các nơi cao và các bàn thờ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và đã bảo Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem rằng: 'Các ngươi phải thờ lạy trước một bàn thờ duy nhất, và đốt [lễ vật] trên đó' sao?
vi.B: Chẳng phải chính Ê-xê-chia này đã dẹp bỏ các nơi cao và các bàn thờ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và bảo Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem: 'Các ngươi phải thờ lạy trước một bàn thờ duy nhất và đốt lễ vật trên đó' sao?
vi.R: Chính Ê-xê-chia đã phá bỏ các nơi thờ phượng trên đồi cao và các bàn thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Hắn bảo dân Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem: 'Các ngươi chỉ được thờ phượng tại một bàn thờ và chỉ đốt lễ vật trên đó mà thôi.'

ko.L: 바로 이 히스기야가 그의 산당들과 그의 제단들을 없애고, 유다와 예루살렘에게 '너희는 한 제단 앞에서 절하고 그 위에서 [제물을] 태워야 한다' 하고 말하지 않았느냐?
ko.B: 바로 이 히스기야가 그의 산당들과 제단들을 없애 버리고, 유다와 예루살렘에게 '너희는 한 제단 앞에서만 절하고 그 위에서만 제물을 태워야 한다' 하고 말하지 않았느냐?
ko.R: 바로 히스기야가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 산꼭대기 제단들과 제단들을 헐어 버렸다. 그리고 유다와 예루살렘 사람들에게 '너희는 오직 한 제단에서만 예배하고, 그 제단에서만 제물을 태워야 한다' 하고 말했다.

pt.L: Não [foi] ele, Ezequias, [quem] removeu os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} altos e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} altares, e disse a Judá e a Jerusalém: 'Diante de um só altar vocês se prostrarão, e sobre ele queimarão [ofertas]'?
pt.B: Não foi esse mesmo Ezequias que acabou com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} altos e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} altares e disse a Judá e a Jerusalém: 'Vocês devem se prostrar diante de um só altar e queimar sobre ele as suas ofertas'?
pt.R: O próprio Ezequias destruiu os santuários {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} no alto dos morros e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} altares. Ele disse ao povo de Judá e de Jerusalém: 'Vocês devem adorar somente em um altar e queimar as suas ofertas somente nele.'

decisions.choice: Hezekiah removed his high places and altars: 2 Kings 18:22
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 18:22 (Isaiah 36:7) the officer's "he" is Yahweh, whose high places Hezekiah removed. Here "he, Hezekiah" points to the king, and "his" to Yahweh named in verse 11. Kings has "before this altar ... in Jerusalem"; Chronicles says "one altar", stressing that only one place of worship was left.

decisions.choice: the Assyrian misreads Hezekiah's reform
decisions.reason: To the Assyrian, closing the shrines looks like an insult to Israel's God. For the writer it was faithfulness (31:1), which makes the taunt ironic.

decisions.choice: make smoke: burn offerings, whether incense or sacrifices
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke on an altar, and is used of incense and of sacrificial portions alike.

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: *Bamot* is "hilltop shrines" at Readable, as in Kings; Readable names Yahweh for the first "his".

decisions.choice: [offerings] / your offerings
decisions.reason: The object of the verb is supplied.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2 Kings 18:22 where the Hebrew is the same
decisions.reason: The Assyrian's charge repeats 2 Kings 18:22 (m1); the Vietnamese Kings wording is reused, with "một bàn thờ duy nhất" for the Hebrew's "one altar".

decisions.choice: os seus altos e os seus altares; um só altar
decisions.reason: The charge keeps the Portuguese of 2 Kings 18:22 at each level (m1), with the deity_pronoun spans on "seus" for Yahweh and Readable's "os santuários do SENHOR no alto dos morros"; Chronicles says "one altar" where Kings says "this altar ... in Jerusalem", and so does the Portuguese: "um só altar".

source.text: הֲלֹ֣א תֵדְע֗וּ מֶ֤ה עָשִׂ֨יתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י וַאֲבוֹתַ֔י לְכֹ֖ל עַמֵּ֣י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת הֲיָכ֣וֹל יָֽכְל֗וּ אֱלֹהֵי֙ גּוֹיֵ֣ הָאֲרָצ֔וֹת לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת־אַרְצָ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: [Do] not you know what have done I and my fathers to all [the] peoples of the lands? Were at all able [the] gods of [the] nations of the lands to deliver their land from my hand?

en.L: Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of the lands at all able to deliver their land from my hand?
en.B: Do you not know what I and my forefathers have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the gods of the nations in those lands ever able to rescue their land from my hand?
en.R: You know what I and the kings before me have done to the peoples of all the other lands. Were the gods of those nations able to save their land from me? Not at all!

es.L: ¿No {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo que yo y mis padres hemos hecho a todos los pueblos de las tierras? ¿Pudieron de algún modo los dioses de las naciones de las tierras librar su tierra de mi mano?
es.B: ¿No {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo que yo y mis antepasados hemos hecho a todos los pueblos de otras tierras? ¿Pudieron alguna vez los dioses de las naciones de esas tierras librar su tierra de mi mano?
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo que yo y los reyes que vinieron antes de mí hemos hecho a los pueblos de todas las demás tierras. ¿Pudieron los dioses de esas naciones salvar su tierra de mí? ¡De ninguna manera!

fr.L: Ne savez-vous pas ce que moi et mes pères avons fait à tous les peuples des pays ? Les dieux des nations des pays ont-ils pu délivrer leur pays de ma main ?
fr.B: Ne savez-vous pas ce que mes ancêtres et moi avons fait à tous les peuples des autres pays ? Les dieux des nations de ces pays ont-ils jamais pu délivrer leur pays de ma main ?
fr.R: Vous savez ce que moi et les rois avant moi avons fait aux peuples de tous les autres pays. Les dieux de ces nations ont-ils pu sauver leur pays de mes mains ? Pas du tout !

sw.L: Je, hamjui yale ambayo mimi na baba zangu tumewafanyia watu wote wa nchi hizi? Je, miungu ya mataifa ya nchi hizo iliweza kweli kuiokoa nchi yao kutoka mkononi mwangu?
sw.B: Je, hamjui yale ambayo mimi na mababu zangu tumewafanyia watu wote wa nchi nyingine? Je, miungu ya mataifa ya nchi hizo iliwahi kuweza kuiokoa nchi yao kutoka mkononi mwangu?
sw.R: Mnajua yale ambayo mimi na wafalme walionitangulia tumewafanyia watu wa nchi nyingine zote. Je, miungu ya mataifa hayo iliweza kuiokoa nchi yao kutoka kwangu? Hata kidogo!

vi.L: Các ngươi không biết ta và tổ phụ ta đã làm gì cho mọi dân tộc của các xứ sao? Các thần của các dân tộc trong các xứ ấy có giải cứu được xứ mình khỏi tay ta chút nào không?
vi.B: Các ngươi không biết ta và tổ tiên ta đã làm gì cho mọi dân tộc ở các xứ khác sao? Các thần của các dân tộc ở những xứ ấy có bao giờ giải cứu được xứ mình khỏi tay ta không?
vi.R: Các ngươi biết ta và các vua trước ta đã làm gì cho các dân tộc ở mọi xứ khác. Các thần của những dân ấy có cứu được xứ mình khỏi tay ta không? Không hề!

ko.L: 나와 내 조상들이 그 땅들의 모든 백성에게 무엇을 했는지 너희가 알지 못하느냐? 그 땅들의 민족들의 신들이 그들의 땅을 내 손에서 정말로 건져 낼 수 있었느냐?
ko.B: 나와 내 조상들이 다른 땅의 모든 백성에게 한 일을 너희가 모르느냐? 그 땅의 민족들의 신들이 자기 땅을 내 손에서 구해 낼 수 있었느냐?
ko.R: 나와 이전 왕들이 다른 모든 나라의 백성에게 무슨 일을 했는지 너희도 알고 있다. 그 민족들의 신들이 자기 땅을 나에게서 구해 낼 수 있었느냐? 전혀 그러지 못했다!

pt.L: Vocês não sabem o que eu e os meus pais fizemos a todos os povos das terras? Puderam de fato os deuses das nações das terras livrar a sua terra da minha mão?
pt.B: Vocês não sabem o que eu e os meus antepassados fizemos a todos os povos de outras terras? Algum dos deuses das nações daquelas terras pôde livrar a sua terra da minha mão?
pt.R: Vocês sabem o que eu e os reis antes de mim fizemos com os povos de todas as outras terras. Os deuses daquelas nações puderam salvar a sua terra de mim? De jeito nenhum!

decisions.choice: the gods of the nations could not deliver their land: 2 Kings 18:33-35; 19:11-12
decisions.reason: The boast gathers what the officer said in 2 Kings 18:33-35 and the letter in 19:11-12. Chronicles leaves out the list of cities (Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim and others) and keeps the argument.

decisions.choice: were they at all able?: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: Repeating the verb sharpens the question, which expects the answer no.

decisions.choice: my fathers: the Assyrian kings before me
decisions.reason: Sennacherib counts the conquests of earlier kings of Assyria as his own line's record.

decisions.choice: a statement, and an added answer
decisions.reason: Readable turns the first question into a statement and spells out the answer the second expects.

source.text: מִ֠י בְּֽכָל־אֱלֹהֵ֞י הַגּוֹיִ֤ם הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱרִ֣ימוּ אֲבוֹתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָכ֔וֹל לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת־עַמּ֖וֹ מִיָּדִ֑י כִּ֤י יוּכַל֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Who among all [the] gods of the nations the these which devoted to destruction my fathers [is there] who was able to deliver his people from my hand, that should be able your God to deliver you from my hand?

en.L: Who among all the gods of these nations that my fathers devoted to destruction [was there] who was able to deliver his people from my hand, that your God should be able to deliver you from my hand?
en.B: Which of all the gods of these nations that my forefathers devoted to destruction was able to rescue its people from my hand? How then could your God rescue you from my hand?
en.R: My ancestors completely destroyed these nations, and not one of their gods could save its people from me. So how could your God save you from me?

es.L: ¿Quién de entre todos los dioses de estas naciones que mis padres destruyeron por completo [hubo] que pudiera librar a su pueblo de mi mano, para que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios pueda librar{{plural_you:los|os}} de mi mano?
es.B: ¿Cuál de todos los dioses de estas naciones que mis antepasados destruyeron por completo pudo librar a su pueblo de mi mano? ¿Cómo podría entonces {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios librar{{plural_you:los|os}} de mi mano?
es.R: Mis antepasados destruyeron por completo estas naciones, y ni uno solo de sus dioses pudo salvar a su pueblo de mí. ¿Cómo podría entonces {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios salvar{{plural_you:los|os}} de mí?

fr.L: Qui, parmi tous les dieux de ces nations que mes pères ont vouées à l’interdit, [y en a-t-il un] qui ait pu délivrer son peuple de ma main, pour que votre Dieu puisse vous délivrer de ma main ?
fr.B: Lequel de tous les dieux de ces nations que mes ancêtres ont vouées à l’interdit a pu délivrer son peuple de ma main ? Comment donc votre Dieu pourrait-il vous délivrer de ma main ?
fr.R: Mes ancêtres ont complètement détruit ces nations, et aucun de leurs dieux n’a pu sauver son peuple de mes mains. Alors comment votre Dieu pourrait-il vous sauver de moi ?

sw.L: Ni nani miongoni mwa miungu yote ya mataifa haya ambayo baba zangu waliyaangamiza kabisa [aliyekuwako] aliyeweza kuwaokoa watu wake kutoka mkononi mwangu, hata Mungu wenu aweze kuwaokoa ninyi kutoka mkononi mwangu?
sw.B: Ni mungu yupi miongoni mwa miungu yote ya mataifa haya, ambayo mababu zangu waliyaangamiza kabisa, aliyeweza kuwaokoa watu wake kutoka mkononi mwangu? Basi Mungu wenu angewezaje kuwaokoa ninyi kutoka mkononi mwangu?
sw.R: Mababu zangu waliyaangamiza kabisa mataifa haya, wala hakuna hata mungu mmoja wao aliyeweza kuwaokoa watu wake kutoka kwangu. Basi Mungu wenu atawezaje kuwaokoa ninyi kutoka kwangu?

vi.L: Trong tất cả các thần của những dân tộc mà tổ phụ ta đã tận diệt, có ai đã giải cứu được dân mình khỏi tay ta, mà Đức Chúa Trời các ngươi lại có thể giải cứu các ngươi khỏi tay ta?
vi.B: Trong tất cả các thần của những dân tộc mà tổ tiên ta đã tận diệt, có thần nào giải cứu được dân mình khỏi tay ta không? Vậy làm sao Đức Chúa Trời các ngươi có thể giải cứu các ngươi khỏi tay ta?
vi.R: Tổ tiên ta đã tiêu diệt hoàn toàn các dân tộc ấy, và không một thần nào của họ cứu được dân mình khỏi tay ta. Vậy làm sao Đức Chúa Trời các ngươi cứu được các ngươi khỏi tay ta?

ko.L: 내 조상들이 진멸한 이 민족들의 모든 신 가운데서 누가 자기 백성을 내 손에서 건져 낼 수 있었기에, 너희 하나님이 너희를 내 손에서 건져 낼 수 있겠느냐?
ko.B: 내 조상들이 진멸한 이 민족들의 모든 신 가운데 어느 신이 자기 백성을 내 손에서 구해 낼 수 있었느냐? 그런데 너희 하나님이 어떻게 너희를 내 손에서 구해 낼 수 있겠느냐?
ko.R: 내 조상들은 이 민족들을 완전히 멸망시켰다. 그 민족들의 신들 가운데 자기 백성을 나에게서 구해 낸 신은 하나도 없었다. 그러니 너희 하나님이 어떻게 너희를 나에게서 구해 낼 수 있겠느냐?

pt.L: Quem, dentre todos os deuses destas nações que os meus pais consagraram à destruição, [houve] que pudesse livrar o seu povo da minha mão, para que o Deus de vocês possa livrá-los da minha mão?
pt.B: Qual de todos os deuses destas nações que os meus antepassados consagraram à destruição pôde livrar o seu povo da minha mão? Como então o Deus de vocês poderia livrá-los da minha mão?
pt.R: Os meus antepassados destruíram completamente estas nações, e nenhum dos seus deuses conseguiu salvar o seu povo de mim. Então como o Deus de vocês poderia salvar vocês de mim?

decisions.choice: who among all the gods ...?: 2 Kings 18:35
decisions.reason: The question follows 2 Kings 18:35 (Isaiah 36:20), "Who among all the gods of the lands ...?". Chronicles says "nations" for "lands" and adds that his fathers devoted them to destruction.

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction: destroyed completely
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for *cherem*, total destruction. In the Assyrian's mouth it is a boast of conquest that left nothing standing.

decisions.choice: your God: the Assyrian puts Israel's God on a level with the others
decisions.reason: Sennacherib treats Yahweh as one more national god. The writer answers this in verse 19 and in what follows.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable split the long question; Readable states the first part as fact.

decisions.choice: consagraram à destruição (L, B); destruíram completamente (R)
decisions.reason: The verb of *cherem* (m2) is "consagrar à destruição" as the Old Testament books set it in Portuguese; Readable says what it did, as the English. The question keeps the Portuguese of 2 Kings 18:35 (m1), "dentre todos os deuses", with Chronicles' "nações".

source.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה אַל־יַשִּׁיא֩ אֶתְכֶ֨ם חִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ וְאַל־יַסִּ֨ית אֶתְכֶ֣ם כָּזֹאת֮ וְאַל־תַּאֲמִ֣ינוּ לוֹ֒ כִּי־לֹ֣א יוּכַ֗ל כָּל־אֱל֨וֹהַ֙ כָּל־גּ֣וֹי וּמַמְלָכָ֔ה לְהַצִּ֥יל עַמּ֛וֹ מִיָּדִ֖י וּמִיַּ֣ד אֲבוֹתָ֑י אַ֚ף כִּ֣י אֱֽלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם לֹא־יַצִּ֥ילוּ אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, let not deceive you Hezekiah, and let him not mislead you like this, and do not believe him; for not has been able any god of any nation and kingdom to deliver his people from my hand and from [the] hand of my fathers. How much less your God will deliver you from my hand!

en.L: And now, do not let Hezekiah deceive you, and do not let him mislead you like this, and do not believe him; for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand and from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God deliver you from my hand!"
en.B: So now, do not let Hezekiah fool you or mislead you like this. Do not believe him. No god of any nation or kingdom has been able to rescue its people from my hand or from the hand of my forefathers. How much less will your God rescue you from my hand!"
en.R: So do not let Hezekiah trick you or lead you astray like this. Do not believe him! No god of any nation or kingdom has been able to save its people from me or from the kings before me. Your God certainly cannot save you from me!"

es.L: Ahora, pues, que no {{plural_you:los|os}} engañe Ezequías, ni {{plural_you:los|os}} seduzca de esta manera, ni le {{plural_you:crean|creáis}}; porque ningún dios de ninguna nación ni reino ha podido librar a su pueblo de mi mano ni de la mano de mis padres. ¡Cuánto menos {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} librará de mi mano!».
es.B: Así que no {{plural_you:se dejen|os dejéis}} engañar por Ezequías ni seducir de esta manera. No le {{plural_you:crean|creáis}}. Ningún dios de ninguna nación ni reino ha podido librar a su pueblo de mi mano ni de la mano de mis antepasados. ¡Cuánto menos {{plural_you:los|os}} librará {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios de mi mano!».
es.R: Así que no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que Ezequías {{plural_you:los|os}} engañe ni {{plural_you:los|os}} lleve por mal camino de esta manera. ¡No le {{plural_you:crean|creáis}}! Ningún dios de ninguna nación ni reino ha podido salvar a su pueblo de mí ni de los reyes que vinieron antes de mí. ¡Mucho menos podrá {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios salvar{{plural_you:los|os}} de mí!».

fr.L: Et maintenant, qu’Ézéchias ne vous trompe pas, et qu’il ne vous égare pas ainsi, et ne le croyez pas ; car aucun dieu d’aucune nation ni d’aucun royaume n’a pu délivrer son peuple de ma main et de la main de mes pères. Combien moins votre Dieu vous délivrera-t-il de ma main ! »
fr.B: Maintenant donc, ne vous laissez pas tromper ni égarer ainsi par Ézéchias. Ne le croyez pas. Aucun dieu d’aucune nation ni d’aucun royaume n’a pu délivrer son peuple de ma main ni de la main de mes ancêtres. Combien moins votre Dieu vous délivrera-t-il de ma main ! »
fr.R: Alors ne vous laissez pas avoir par Ézéchias et ne le laissez pas vous égarer ainsi. Ne le croyez pas ! Aucun dieu d’aucune nation ni d’aucun royaume n’a pu sauver son peuple de moi ou des rois avant moi. Votre Dieu ne pourra certainement pas vous sauver de moi ! »

sw.L: Basi sasa Hezekia asiwadanganye, wala asiwapotoshe hivi, wala msimwamini; kwa maana hakuna mungu wa taifa lolote wala wa ufalme wowote aliyeweza kuwaokoa watu wake kutoka mkononi mwangu na kutoka mkononi mwa baba zangu. Sembuse Mungu wenu atawaokoa ninyi kutoka mkononi mwangu!"
sw.B: Basi sasa msikubali Hezekia awadanganye wala awapotoshe hivi. Msimwamini. Hakuna mungu wa taifa lolote wala wa ufalme wowote aliyeweza kuwaokoa watu wake kutoka mkononi mwangu au kutoka mkononi mwa mababu zangu. Sembuse Mungu wenu atawaokoa kutoka mkononi mwangu!"
sw.R: Kwa hiyo msikubali Hezekia awadanganye wala awapotoshe hivi. Msimwamini! Hakuna mungu wa taifa lolote wala wa ufalme wowote aliyeweza kuwaokoa watu wake kutoka kwangu au kutoka kwa wafalme walionitangulia. Hakika Mungu wenu hawezi kuwaokoa kutoka kwangu!"

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, đừng để Ê-xê-chia lừa dối các ngươi, đừng để hắn dụ dỗ các ngươi như thế, và đừng tin hắn; vì không thần nào của bất cứ dân tộc hay vương quốc nào đã có thể giải cứu dân mình khỏi tay ta và khỏi tay tổ phụ ta. Huống chi Đức Chúa Trời các ngươi giải cứu các ngươi khỏi tay ta!"
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, đừng để Ê-xê-chia lừa gạt hay dụ dỗ các ngươi như thế. Đừng tin hắn. Không thần nào của bất cứ dân tộc hay vương quốc nào đã giải cứu được dân mình khỏi tay ta hay khỏi tay tổ tiên ta. Huống chi Đức Chúa Trời các ngươi lại giải cứu được các ngươi khỏi tay ta!"
vi.R: Vậy đừng để Ê-xê-chia lừa các ngươi hay dẫn các ngươi lạc lối như thế. Đừng tin hắn! Không thần nào của bất cứ dân tộc hay vương quốc nào đã cứu được dân mình khỏi tay ta hay khỏi tay các vua trước ta. Đức Chúa Trời các ngươi chắc chắn không thể cứu các ngươi khỏi tay ta!"

ko.L: 그러니 이제 히스기야가 너희를 속이지 못하게 하고, 이처럼 너희를 꾀지 못하게 하여라. 그를 믿지 마라. 어떤 민족이나 나라의 어떤 신도 자기 백성을 내 손과 내 조상들의 손에서 건져 낼 수 없었다. 하물며 너희 하나님이 너희를 내 손에서 건져 내겠느냐!"
ko.B: 그러니 이제 히스기야에게 속지 말고, 이처럼 꾀임을 당하지도 마라. 그를 믿지 마라. 어떤 민족이나 나라의 신도 자기 백성을 내 손이나 내 조상들의 손에서 구해 내지 못했다. 하물며 너희 하나님이 너희를 내 손에서 구해 낼 수 있겠느냐!"
ko.R: 그러니 히스기야에게 속지 마라. 그가 이렇게 너희를 엉뚱한 길로 이끌지 못하게 하여라. 그를 믿지 마라! 어떤 민족이나 나라의 신도 자기 백성을 나나 이전 왕들에게서 구해 내지 못했다. 너희 하나님도 분명히 너희를 나에게서 구해 내지 못할 것이다!"

pt.L: E agora, que Ezequias não os engane, nem os iluda assim, e não creiam nele; porque nenhum deus de nação alguma ou reino pôde livrar o seu povo da minha mão e da mão dos meus pais. Quanto menos o Deus de vocês os livrará da minha mão!"
pt.B: Portanto, não deixem que Ezequias os engane nem os iluda desse modo. Não acreditem nele! Nenhum deus de qualquer nação ou reino conseguiu livrar o seu povo da minha mão nem da mão dos meus antepassados. Muito menos o Deus de vocês os livrará da minha mão!"
pt.R: Por isso não deixem que Ezequias engane vocês ou os leve para o caminho errado desse jeito. Não acreditem nele! Nenhum deus de qualquer nação ou reino conseguiu salvar o seu povo de mim ou dos reis antes de mim. O Deus de vocês com certeza não pode salvar vocês de mim!"

decisions.choice: do not let Hezekiah deceive you: 2 Kings 18:29
decisions.reason: The same verb for "deceive" as in 2 Kings 18:29 (Isaiah 36:14); Chronicles adds "mislead" from 2 Kings 18:32 and "do not believe him".

decisions.choice: how much less your God: an argument from the greater to the lesser
decisions.reason: If no god of any nation could save its people, the Assyrian argues, Judah's God can do even less. The verb with "your God" is plural, as if the speaker thought of Israel's God as one more set of gods (compare verse 19).

decisions.choice: any god: the singular word for a god
decisions.reason: The Assyrian uses the less common singular word for a god, making his claim cover each god one by one.

decisions.choice: fool (Balanced); trick (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 18:29 at the same levels.

decisions.choice: "no se dejen engañar" (B); "no dejen que ... los engañe" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Spanish 2 Kings 18:29 at the same levels.

decisions.choice: engane (every level), iluda (L, B), leve para o caminho errado (R)
decisions.reason: "Que Ezequias não os engane" is the Portuguese of 2 Kings 18:29 at Literal, and "Não deixem que Ezequias os engane" at Balanced and Readable (m1); the second verb is "iludir", as in verse 11. Readable says "leve para o caminho errado" for "lead astray".

source.text: וְעוֹד֙ דִּבְּר֣וּ עֲבָדָ֔יו עַל־יְהוָ֖ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ עַבְדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And still spoke his servants against Yahweh the God and against Hezekiah his servant.

en.L: And his servants spoke still more against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God and against Hezekiah {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave.
en.B: His officials said still more against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God and against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Hezekiah.
en.R: Sennacherib's officials said even more things against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God and against Hezekiah, who served {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y sus siervos hablaron aún más contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios y contra Ezequías {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} siervo.
es.B: Sus funcionarios dijeron todavía más cosas contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios y contra {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} siervo Ezequías.
es.R: Los funcionarios de Senaquerib dijeron todavía más cosas contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios y contra Ezequías, que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servía.

fr.L: Et ses serviteurs parlèrent encore contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu et contre Ézéchias, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} esclave.
fr.B: Ses officiers parlèrent encore contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu et contre {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur Ézéchias.
fr.R: Les officiers de Sennachérib ont dit encore d’autres choses contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu et contre Ézéchias, qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servait.

sw.L: Na watumishi wake wakazidi kusema dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu na dhidi ya Hezekia mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Maafisa wake walisema mengine zaidi dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu na dhidi ya mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Hezekia.
sw.R: Maafisa wa Senakeribu walisema mambo mengi zaidi dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu na dhidi ya Hezekia, aliyemtumikia.

vi.L: Các đầy tớ của hắn còn nói thêm nghịch cùng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời và nghịch cùng Ê-xê-chia, đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Các quan của hắn còn nói thêm nhiều điều nghịch cùng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời và nghịch cùng Ê-xê-chia, đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Các quan của San-chê-ríp còn nói thêm nhiều điều chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời và chống lại Ê-xê-chia, đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그의 신하들이 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 그분의 종 히스기야를 거슬러 더 말했다.
ko.B: 산헤립의 관리들은 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 그분의 종 히스기야를 거슬러 더 많은 말을 했다.
ko.R: 산헤립의 관리들은 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 그분을 섬기는 히스기야를 헐뜯는 말을 더 많이 했다.

pt.L: E os servos dele falaram ainda mais contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus e contra Ezequias, o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} escravo.
pt.B: Os oficiais dele disseram ainda mais coisas contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus e contra Ezequias, o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} servo.
pt.R: Os oficiais de Senaqueribe disseram ainda mais coisas contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus e contra Ezequias, que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} servia.

decisions.choice: still more: the writer cuts the speeches short
decisions.reason: The writer gives only a sample of what was said (compare 2 Kings 18:19-35) and sums up the rest.

decisions.choice: his servants ... his servant: Sennacherib's officials against Yahweh's servant
decisions.reason: The same word names the Assyrian king's officials and Hezekiah as Yahweh's servant, setting the two masters side by side.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: *'Eved* for Hezekiah as Yahweh's servant follows the rule for "my servant David"; for Sennacherib's envoys it is "servants" at Literal and "officials" at the other levels.

decisions.choice: "su siervo" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Hezekiah as the LORD's servant is "siervo" at every level, Literal included, as God's servants are in Spanish Kings.

decisions.choice: "son esclave" (Literal); "son serviteur" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: God's servant as in French Kings: "esclave" at Literal, "serviteur" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: mtumishi wake (every level)
decisions.reason: Hezekiah as the LORD's servant is "mtumishi" at every level, as the terms notes set for God's servants; the Assyrian king's men are "watumishi" (L) and "maafisa" (B, R).

decisions.choice: "các đầy tớ của hắn" (L), "các quan" (B, R) for Sennacherib's men; "Ê-xê-chia, đầy tớ của Ngài" at every level
decisions.reason: God's servant is "đầy tớ" at every level, Literal included; the king's men are officials at Balanced and Readable, as the Samuel note sets.

decisions.choice: os servos (L), os oficiais (B, R) of Sennacherib; o seu escravo (L), o seu servo (B), que o servia (R) for Hezekiah
decisions.reason: The Old Testament terms give the word "escravo" at Literal and "servo" at Balanced and Readable for a servant of God, as the English "slave" and "servant"; the Assyrian's envoys keep "servos" (L) and "oficiais" (B, R), as in verse 9. "Dele" makes clear whose officials they are, where "seus" could be read as God's.

source.text: וּסְפָרִ֣ים כָּתַ֔ב לְחָרֵ֕ף לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֵֽאמֹ֨ר עָלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כֵּֽאלֹהֵ֞י גּוֹיֵ֤ הָאֲרָצוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־הִצִּ֤ילוּ עַמָּם֙ מִיָּדִ֔י כֵּ֣ן לֹֽא־יַצִּ֞יל אֱלֹהֵ֧י יְחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עַמּ֖וֹ מִיָּדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And letters he wrote to taunt Yahweh God of Israel and to say against him, saying, like [the] gods of [the] nations of the lands which not delivered their people from my hand, so not will deliver [the] God of Hezekiah his people from my hand.

en.L: And he wrote letters to taunt {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel and to speak against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Like the gods of the nations of the lands, which have not delivered their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not deliver {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people from my hand."
en.B: He also wrote letters to insult {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, and to speak against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Just as the gods of the nations of other lands have not rescued their people from my hand, so Hezekiah's God will not rescue {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people from my hand."
en.R: Sennacherib also wrote letters that insulted {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. He wrote this against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "The gods of the other nations could not save their people from me. In the same way, Hezekiah's God will not save {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people from me."

es.L: Y escribió cartas para afrentar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, y para hablar contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, diciendo: «Como los dioses de las naciones de las tierras no libraron a su pueblo de mi mano, así el Dios de Ezequías no librará a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo de mi mano».
es.B: También escribió cartas para insultar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, y hablar contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: «Así como los dioses de las naciones de otras tierras no libraron a su pueblo de mi mano, tampoco el Dios de Ezequías librará a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo de mi mano».
es.R: Senaquerib también escribió cartas que insultaban {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel. Escribió esto contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: «Los dioses de las demás naciones no pudieron salvar a su pueblo de mí. De la misma manera, el Dios de Ezequías no salvará a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo de mí».

fr.L: Et il écrivit des lettres pour insulter {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, et pour parler contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, en disant : « Comme les dieux des nations des pays, qui n’ont pas délivré leur peuple de ma main, ainsi le Dieu d’Ézéchias ne délivrera pas {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple de ma main. »
fr.B: Il écrivit aussi des lettres pour insulter {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, et pour parler contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : « Tout comme les dieux des nations des autres pays n’ont pas délivré leur peuple de ma main, ainsi le Dieu d’Ézéchias ne délivrera pas {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple de ma main. »
fr.R: Sennachérib a aussi écrit des lettres qui insultaient {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël. Il a écrit ceci contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : « Les dieux des autres nations n’ont pas pu sauver leur peuple de moi. De la même manière, le Dieu d’Ézéchias ne sauvera pas {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple de moi. »

sw.L: Akaandika barua ili kumtukana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa Israeli na kusema dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akisema, "Kama miungu ya mataifa ya nchi hizi isivyowaokoa watu wao kutoka mkononi mwangu, vivyo hivyo Mungu wa Hezekia hatawaokoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kutoka mkononi mwangu."
sw.B: Pia aliandika barua za kumtukana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, na kusema dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: "Kama vile miungu ya mataifa ya nchi nyingine isivyowaokoa watu wao kutoka mkononi mwangu, vivyo hivyo Mungu wa Hezekia hatawaokoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kutoka mkononi mwangu."
sw.R: Senakeribu aliandika pia barua zilizomtukana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli. Aliandika hivi dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: "Miungu ya mataifa mengine haikuweza kuwaokoa watu wao kutoka kwangu. Vivyo hivyo Mungu wa Hezekia hatawaokoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kutoka kwangu."

vi.L: Hắn cũng viết thư để nhạo báng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, và nói nghịch cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rằng: "Như các thần của các dân tộc trong các xứ đã không giải cứu được dân mình khỏi tay ta, thì Đức Chúa Trời của Ê-xê-chia cũng sẽ không giải cứu được dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khỏi tay ta."
